title: The Great Train Robbery (1963)
hook: Who vanished with £2.6 million from a moving train?
headline: Heist that stunned a nation

beats.label: THE CASE
beats.line: On August 8, 1963, a Royal Mail train was stopped near Bridego Railway Bridge.

beats.label: CLUE 1
beats.line: Robbers used a flatbed truck to block the line and forced the driver to uncouple the locomotive.

beats.label: CLUE 2
beats.line: Investigators found a large amount of used banknotes, later linked to several suspects.

beats.label: THE TWIST
beats.line: A gang member claimed the loot was hidden in a farmhouse, but police found nothing.

end.line: Where do you think the money vanished?

description: A quick look at the baffling 1963 Great Train Robbery and lingering mysteries.

facts.claim: The robbery occurred on August 8, 1963, near Bridego Railway Bridge in Kendal, England
£2.6 million in used banknotes were stolen, equivalent to about £55 million today
The gang used a flatbed truck to block the line and force the driver to uncouple the locomotive
Police identified 12 suspects linked to the stolen cash
In 2020 a former gang member claimed the loot was hidden in a rural farmhouse, but no money was recovered

bad: contradicted: £2.6 million was taken from the train (spravne: £2.61 million)
